reviewer: independent adversarial reviewer; authored neither the contract nor the checker
verdict: REJECT - CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, on ONE blocking finding. This is a far narrower rejection than the v5 REJECT it succeeds, and it should be read that way. Everything c2-plan-stage-schema.v6 set out to do, it does, and I verified it by execution rather than by reading: I could not break jx_canon's injectivity in 82,368 distinct tokens of hostile and random input; the primitive genuinely stands alone; I independently reproduced IR-C2V5-01 against the pinned v5 and confirmed v6's widened scan names the exact site (check-c2-v5.py line 1815) that v5's own scan called clean; my own exhaustive sweep over the candidate is 137 cases and ZERO admitted, with zero genuine collateral; the 109-row --selftest, which no prior session had observed end to end, ran to completion GREEN under me on the reviewed bytes with 0 escapes and 0 counter-only rows; and all 13 required dependents exit 0. It is nevertheless REJECTED because a single 18-byte edit to the candidate document, with no source modification, still reaches exit 0 and a full green banner while placing a JSON number at the one key whose integer-ness this checker explicitly enforces. The candidate is parsed with json.loads and no duplicate-key refusal, so a duplicate key shadows the checked leaf: the parsed object is byte-for-byte the original, the run is green, the banner still certifies '105 integer leaves of THIS document bound ... with no unbound bucket', and the document of record carries 6.0 at 'version'. That is one JSON edit to a fully green run, which is this corpus's own bright line for a blocking finding, and the defence is already implemented and selftested by a sibling checker in the same directory. CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A; this review changes no status.
verdictRule: A finding is BLOCKING when a single edit to the candidate, with no modification of checker source, produces exit 0 - the rule freeze section 7.4 applies and the rule under which IR-C2V4-01 and IR-C2V5-01 were graded. IR-C2V6-01 meets it by execution. Findings that are honestly scoped out by a published rule, or that I could not drive to exit 0, are recorded as non-blocking however uncomfortable they are.

blockers.title: A duplicate JSON key shadows a bound leaf: one 18-byte edit puts a JSON number at 'version' and the run is fully green, while the banner certifies that every integer leaf of THIS document is bound with no unbound bucket

minimalReproduction.edit: insert one line, '  "version": 6.0,', immediately BEFORE the existing '  "version": 6,' at the document root
minimalReproduction.banner: full green, including 'L2c candidate-document binding: 105 integer leaves of THIS document bound to a value this run measured or to a verified pinned byte, with no unbound bucket; 945 hostile spelling and value-drift and control probes at those leaves, of which 0 were admitted'

blockers.whyTheCheckerCannotSeeIt: main() does candidate = json.loads(path.read_text()) with no object_pairs_hook. CPython's json keeps the LAST occurrence of a duplicated key, so the parsed object is byte-for-byte IDENTICAL to the parse of the unedited document - I verified that equality directly. Every layer of v6 - L2c's leaf enumeration, the C2V6-UNBOUND totality check, the identity rule, the hostile-spelling probes - operates on that parsed object. Nothing in the checker reads the candidate's raw bytes; the only read_bytes calls are for the 16 pinned inputs and for the checker's own source.
whyThisIsBlockingAndNotAdvisory: It meets the corpus's own bright line exactly: one JSON edit, zero bytes of Python, exit 0, full green banner. That is the rule under which IR-C2V4-01 and IR-C2V5-01 were graded BLOCKING.

It falsifies a published headline claim, not a marginal one. v6MeasuredCountersRule says 'Every integer leaf of THIS document -- not only this block -- is bound ... There is no unbound bucket: a leaf no layer binds is itself a named finding, so narrowing the binding table fails closed.' After the edit the document's BYTES contain a numeric leaf that no layer binds, the leaf count is still published as 105, and C2V6-UNBOUND does not fire. The totality is over the parse, not over the document.

The float lands at 'version', the one position whose integer-ness this checker enforces by an explicit named rule - 'candidate must declare version 6 superseding 5 as JSON integers; a float or boolean spelling is refused by the same rule this successor exists to enforce'. That rule does not fire, on a document that contains exactly the spelling it forbids.
The recording obligation in freeze section 7.2 binds BYTES. Here the bytes of record and the object certified are different documents, and the divergence is invisible from the banner.

It is not an exotic reviewer invention. check-trusted-request-context-v3.py, in this same directory, already parses through an object_pairs_hook that raises DuplicateKeyError, and retains 'duplicate JSON key' as a scored selftest case. The defence is known here, deployed here, and tested here - and the artifact whose whole thesis is 'a spelling enumeration cannot close a class, build one primitive and route everything through it' does not have it.

It is orthogonal to the primitive. jx_canon is not defeated; it never sees the shadowed value. That is precisely why no amount of strengthening the comparison primitive closes this, and why it needs its own repair.
blockers.whatWouldDischargeIt: Parse the candidate with an object_pairs_hook that refuses duplicate keys and emit a named finding, and add a retained selftest row for it, exactly as check-trusted-request-context-v3.py already does. This is a small, local change; it does not touch the primitive, any layer, or any published counter. I would expect a successor to be a few lines plus one row, not a redesign.
blockers.controlForVacuity: The byte-identical control (P8) exits 0, and the same edit with the float placed AFTER the real key (P2), so that the parse keeps 6.0, is refused by FOUR independently named findings - C2V6 identity, C2V6-UNBOUND, C2V6-TYPE naming the position and the spelling, and C2V6-CANDIDATE. The checker's guards are strong; they are simply downstream of the parser.

nonBlockingObservations.title: A new candidate leaf whose value is a FLOAT is admitted to a green run; only INTEGER leaves are enumerated by the unbound-leaf guard
nonBlockingObservations.measured: Adding '"reviewerInjectedLeaf": 17,' to the document root is refused by C2V6-UNBOUND (exit 1). Adding '"reviewerInjectedLeaf": 17.0,' - the same key, a float - exits 0 with a full green banner.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: The rule is honestly scoped: v6MeasuredCountersRule and the L2c blind spot both say the binding covers INTEGER leaves, and a float leaf is outside the stated claim rather than a violation of it.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItStillMatters: The L2c blind-spot entry names STRINGS as the neighbouring gap and does not mention numbers at all, while the entire artifact exists because of int/float equivalence. That is the same shape the author correctly criticised in v5 - a residual that points away from the live hazard. The disclosure would be materially better if it said 'a non-integer scalar of this document, including a JSON number, is bound only where the checker gates it explicitly'.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The adoption instructions in the checker docstring name two functions that do not exist, and both documents attribute a refusal to jx_sorted that it does not perform
nonBlockingObservations.measured: check-c2-v6.py lines 98-99 instruct an adopter to 'Replace sorted/min/max over wire values with jx_sorted/jx_min/jx_max, which REFUSE a heterogeneous JSON type set instead of ordering it.' jx_min and jx_max do not exist anywhere in the file - I checked by attribute lookup on the extracted region and by grep over the whole checker; the only occurrences of those names are the docstring itself. Separately, jx_sorted([1, 1.0]) returns [1, 1.0]: it ORDERS the heterogeneous set (by canonical token, which is safe and type-separating, but is not a refusal). The function that refuses is jx_sorted_homogeneous, which returns (None, 'a mixed JSON type set [integer, number] cannot be ordered; law 18 rejects the type before the content is compared').
nonBlockingObservations.note: The CONTRACT document's adoption step 3 names jx_sorted and jx_sorted_homogeneous correctly, so the wrong names are confined to the checker docstring; but the contract still says both of them REFUSE, and only one does.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItMatters: Adoption is one of this artifact's two declared deliverables and claim 6 asks directly whether the instructions are sufficient. An adopter following the checker's own normative 'WHAT AN ADOPTING CHECKER MUST DO' verbatim gets a NameError. The portability claim that IS verified - 0 free names outside the declared boundary - is verified structurally every run; the instructions telling a reader how to USE the region are not checked at all by anything.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: It is a documentation defect. The primitive itself is sound and I verified it standalone.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The anti-recurrence check described alongside the mid-review edit is not present in the bytes
nonBlockingObservations.measured: The account relayed with the corrected assertion said the author 'added a check that every declared subject string actually occurs in the source'. The text diff between the dispatched and reviewed checkers contains exactly one changed string constant and nothing else, the blanked-constant ASTs are identical, and the use sites of the three mutation tables are line-for-line the same in both files. No such check exists in either version.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItMatters: The defect that was corrected is an assertion table drifting out of sync with the guard text it asserts. Nothing detects that class today except running the full 109-row matrix to termination - which is the thing this corpus has repeatedly not done. A three-line check that every declared subject substring occurs somewhere in the checker's own source would close it, and it would also have caught OBS-C2V6-02's jx_min/jx_max, which is the same failure: naming a string that does not exist.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Bare truthiness is an int/float/bool equivalence path that the 28-row operator space omits and that L4 does not model
nonBlockingObservations.measured: bool(1) == bool(1.0) == bool(True) and bool(0) == bool(0.0) == bool(False), so 'if x:' has exactly the int/float/bool equivalence semantics the table exists to enumerate. OPERATOR_SPACE has 28 rows and none of them is a truthiness row; _hazard_pairs models Compare, set-algebra BinOp, Subscript, Set/Dict/SetComp/DictComp construction and operator-style Calls, and does not treat ast.If, ast.While, ast.IfExp, ast.BoolOp, ast.Assert, unary not, or comprehension-ifs as sites. Using v6's OWN taint model and non-numeric proofs I measured the bare-truthiness sites on a tainted operand: 24 in check-c2-v6.py, 27 in check-c2-v5.py, 42 in check-c2-v4.py. Separately, '%d' % 1 == '%d' % 1.0 == '%d' % True is a stringification coercion also absent from the table.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: I inspected all 24 sites in check-c2-v6.py and none of them is a wire NUMBER: they are containers and AST objects ('not rows', 'not path', 'not fields', 'not candidates', "row['v5FullyGreen']"), where truthiness is emptiness rather than numeric value. I could not drive any of them to a false accept.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItStillMatters: The claim in both the module docstring and the contract is that the table enumerates the operator space - 'Every Python operation below has int/float/bool equivalence semantics'. It does not, and the gap is inherited by every adopter told to copy wire_comparison_scan and drive its count to zero.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Two documented properties of the primitive are slightly stronger than the code
items: 'no numeric operator is ever executed on a wire operand' (module docstring) is not literally true: jx_order runs a < b and jx_int_in_range runs low <= value <= high. Both are sound, because every operand is type-gated to the SAME JSON type first, so no coercion is reachable - but the accurate statement is 'no comparison between operands of different JSON type is ever executed', not 'no numeric operator runs'.

jx_in_domain is documented 'Total. True when jx_canon will succeed.' For a Python int with more than 4300 decimal digits jx_in_domain returns True and jx_canon raises ValueError from str(value), under CPython's int-to-str digit limit. Not reachable from the wire, because json.loads raises on such a literal for the same reason, and ValueError is in MALFORMED_SHAPE_EXCEPTIONS.

nonBlockingObservations.title: jx_order disagrees with jx_equal on signed zero and on NaN
nonBlockingObservations.measured: jx_order(0.0, -0.0) returns 0 (comparable and equal) while jx_equal(0.0, -0.0) is False. jx_order(nan, 1.0) also returns 0, because neither a < b nor b < a holds, so jx_le(nan, 1.0) and jx_ge(nan, 1.0) are both True. The ordering relation therefore reports 'equal' at pairs the canonical equality reports distinct, and NaN is order-equal to every float.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: Both operands must already share the JSON type 'number' to reach that branch, and I found no path in check-c2-v6.py that puts a wire float through jx_order, jx_le or jx_ge - the candidate's numeric leaves are gated as integers. A bare NaN IS reachable from the wire, since json.loads accepts the non-RFC NaN token, but I drove NaN and Infinity into the candidate and both are refused (exit 1).
nonBlockingObservations.note: The blind-spot list discloses the NaN divergence for EQUALITY and states the primitive is looser there by exactly one pair. It does not disclose that ORDERING inherits the divergence, nor the signed-zero ordering case.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The bare-digit banner detector is a token-shape heuristic and is bypassed by gluing a digit to a letter
nonBlockingObservations.measured: banner_digit_tokens fires on '57', '1/1/1/0', 'measured in 68 seconds'. It does NOT fire on 'measured in 68s', 'sweep57 leaves', 'x57', or numbers spelled as words, because any token containing a letter is exempt.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: The claim as worded - a BARE digit run in template text is structurally refused - is true, the detector is genuinely probed with a known-positive that does fire, and I verified the real templates carry 0 literal digit tokens. This is a note on the strength of the instrument, not a defect in it.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The incomplete selftest is not carried as a residual in the artifact
nonBlockingObservations.measured: The contract carries 7 residuals and 4 knownLimitations entries. None of them records that the 109-row matrix had not been observed end to end. RES-C2V6-03 is about not re-running the PREDECESSOR's matrix, which is a different gap. Searching the document for 'did not complete', 'incomplete', 'unobserved', 'end-to-end' and '109' returns nothing.
nonBlockingObservations.note: The dispatch described 'ten retained residuals, including the incomplete selftest'. I count 7 residuals, or 11 including knownLimitations, and the incomplete selftest is not among them - the disclosure was made to the reviewer in prose but was never written into the artifact. This observation is now largely moot for the artifact going forward, because I have run the matrix to completion and it is green; but as shipped, the residual list overstated its own completeness.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The dirty-base refusal reports a denominator that does not match the green run's row count
nonBlockingObservations.measured: --selftest over a dirty base prints 'zero of 96 mutations executed', because total = len(CONTRACT_MUTATIONS) + len(SOURCE_MUTATIONS) + len(SCAN_MUTATIONS) = 23 + 65 + 8. A green run reports 109 rows, which additionally counts the 4 parsed-JSON-root rows, 6 v4-differential rows and 3 v5-differential rows. Both numbers are honest; a reader comparing them will think 13 rows went missing.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The dict-key blind spot is accurately stated and IS unreachable from the wire as claimed - but a neighbouring construction-time loss is reachable and is not named
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: The disclosure is correct: json.loads produces only string object keys, so {1: 'a', True: 'b', 1.0: 'c'} cannot arrive from a parse, and I confirmed the checker installs no object_hook that could create one. jx_keyset and jx_unique do close the sequence case - I measured len(jx_keyset([1, 1.0, True])) == 3 and len(jx_keyset([0, 0.0, -0.0, False])) == 4 against a host len({1, 1.0, True}) of 1. What the entry does not name is that the SAME parser loses information at construction in a way that IS wire-reachable - duplicate keys, silently collapsed to the last occurrence. That is IR-C2V6-01, and it belongs in this blind spot as well as in the repair.

1_thePrimitive.verdict: UPHELD. I could not break injectivity or round-tripping.
1_thePrimitive.whatIRan: The delimited region was extracted verbatim into a bare module and attacked standalone. Hand-built hostile corpus of 74 values covering lone surrogates, U+10FFFF, NUL, BOM, NFC vs NFD ('e-acute' precomposed vs combining), strings that imitate canonical tokens ('i1:1', 's1:a', '5:hello', 's3:abcs3:def', '1\x00:x'), -0.0 vs 0.0, +/-inf, NaN and -NaN, 2**63, 10**30, 1e16 vs 1e16+2, nested empties ([[], [[]]] vs [[[]], []]), and objects with integer-like string keys: 0 round-trip failures, 0 collisions. Exhaustive frame-forging over an alphabet of framing characters (':', digits, tag letters, 's1:a', '5:') across all arrays of length 0-2, 183 cases: 0 forged collisions, 0 round-trip failures. Random deep fuzz of 300,000 generated values: 82,368 distinct tokens, 0 round-trip failures, 0 collisions.
1_thePrimitive.whyTheFramingHolds: The length prefix is read from between the tag and the FIRST colon after it, and the payload is then consumed by count, so payload content can never be reinterpreted as a frame boundary. Cross-type collisions are impossible by distinct tag. Within-type injectivity reduces to str() on int, repr() on float (shortest round-tripping, so distinct floats give distinct text, and -0.0 gives '-0.0'), identity on str, and self-delimiting concatenation for arrays and sorted key-value pairs for objects.
1_thePrimitive.typeExactness: jx_type decides boolean BEFORE integer and uses 'type(x) is C' throughout, so no subclass is mistaken for its base - I confirmed int, str, list and dict subclasses are all refused as 'unsupported', and Decimal(1), Fraction(1,1) and complex(1,0) all raise JxDomainError and are not equal to 1.
1_thePrimitive.theOneDivergenceIsAsDeclared: NaN is made reflexive, which is correct for an admission gate; signed zero is treated as distinct, which is stricter. Both are published.

2_theOperatorSpace.verdict: UPHELD WITH ONE OMISSION FOUND. See OBS-C2V6-04 (bare truthiness, and '%d' stringification).
2_theOperatorSpace.theContainerHalf: CONFIRMED and it is the strongest part of the table. len({1, 1.0, True}) is 1 on this host; len(jx_keyset([1, 1.0, True])) is 3 and len(jx_keyset([0, 0.0, -0.0, False])) is 4. jx_unique([1, 1.0, True]) is 3. jx_keyset does give 3 everywhere I could reach it, and it correctly REFUSES a tuple with JxDomainError rather than silently deduping ({(1,1),(1,1.0)} has length 1 on the host).
2_theOperatorSpace.alsoChecked: jx_bind refuses all six hostile spellings of a published 1 with a named reason; jx_exact_int(True, 1) and jx_exact_int(1.0, 1) are False; jx_int_in_range(True, 0, 5) is False; jx_sum_int([1, True]) refuses by name.
